name: North America: California, Central Coast
court: NORTH AMERICA - UNITED STATES - CALIFORNIA - CENTRAL COAST

outcome.intro: After studying this section, a student will know selected counties of the Central Coast of California and the major AVAs within them. Students will know basic wine labeling laws and understand the relationship of climate to the grape varieties grown.
outcome.certified: After studying this section, a candidate will dive deeper into selected counties of the Central Coast of California and the major AVAs within them. Certified Sommeliers will know iconic producers and vineyards and be able to recommend and sell food pairings to a guest.

rows.intro: Coastal counties south of the San Francisco Bay and north of the city of Santa Barbara.
rows.certified: Identify on a map: Monterey, San Luis Obispo, Santa Barbara

rows.intro: Monterey County; San Luis Obispo: Paso Robles AVA; Santa Barbara County; *Know geographical locations in relation to each other and the major AVA of San Luis Obispo.
rows.certified: Monterey County: Santa Lucia Highlands AVA; San Luis Obispo: Paso Robles AVA; Santa Barbara County: Sta. Rita Hills AVA, Santa Maria Valley AVA, Santa Ynez Valley AVA, Happy Canyon AVA; *Match AVAs to counties.

rows.intro: Monterey and Santa Barbara are generally cool maritime; the closer to the coast, the cooler it is. Paso Robles is warm continental with large diurnal shifts.
rows.certified: Paso Robles AVA and Happy Canyon AVA are warm climate; the others listed above are cool Pinot Noir and Chardonnay growing regions.

rows.intro: Monterey has a northwest-to-southeast mountain range creating a cool wind tunnel. Paso Robles is blocked by mountains to the west with only a small gap in the range. Santa Barbara has an east-to-west mountain range creating a cool wind tunnel and fog.
Often extensive use of new French and sometimes American oak barrels for both red and white wines. Malolactic fermentation often employed when making white wines, especially Chardonnay.

rows.certified: Match the grape varieties to the major AVAs.

rows.intro: Pinot Noir, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Zinfandel, Syrah
rows.certified: Match the grape varieties to the major AVAs.

rows.intro: 75% minimum grape variety; 85% minimum for AVA; 95% minimum for vintage; 95% minimum for single vineyard
rows.certified: 100% for Estate bottling; must be in the same county.
Knowledge of iconic producers and vineyards are expected at Certified Sommelier level. Some examples include: Ridge, Justin, Au Bon Climat, and others.
